newsitem.title: FRANCE: France honours U.S. actor Charlton Heston.
newsitem.headline: France honours U.S. actor Charlton Heston.

text.p: Veteran U.S. film actor Charlton Heston received France's highest cultural honour on Monday in recognition of a career spanning more than five decades.

"I've played a knight several times before, but I've never been made one," Heston, 73, quipped after French Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy made him a Commander in the Order of Arts and Letters.
The star of such screen classics as Ben Hur, El Cid and Plant of the Apes said he was "honoured to receive this honour in a country that values art as deeply as France does".
Heston's wife, Lydia Clarke Heston, as at his side as he received the award on their 50th wedding anniversary.
France, which prides itself on the vigour of its film industry, has in recent years given medals to such Hollywood stars as Sharon Stone and Sylvester Stallone.
